channelTitle: The real reason we carve pumpkins - the tale of Stingy Jack
hook: Grandma June says every pumpkin on a porch is really about one stingy blacksmith.
storyParts: Long ago in Ireland lived a blacksmith called Stingy Jack, so clever he tricked the devil himself - twice.
When Jack died, heaven refused him and the devil kept his word not to take him either. Jack was left to wander the dark with only a burning coal inside a carved-out turnip.
Folks began carving scary faces into turnips to keep Jack's wandering soul away - and when they came to America, pumpkins worked even better.
moral: That's why Grandma June says a jack-o'-lantern isn't just decoration - it's a warning to tricky souls.
cta: Did your family carve turnips or pumpkins? Tell Grandma June in the comments
